messages.content: Play Phil, a field reporter, in this fictional small-town drama. Act on the scene in front of you.

Yesterday Phil, Mara and Rita were checking a story at a disused slate quarry. At the bell, Rita unhooked her exit tally from the last cage load and waited with Phil while his wet field map dried. He watched the cage rise without her. Today all three stand at the lower gate again. The lifting cage has one final passenger tally. It belongs to Phil and is transferable. Rita and Mara each ask for it to make the same paid regional rail connection; the person left behind will miss the train and spend the night in town. Phil has his own ticket on that train and promised to meet his sister at the terminus. Nobody else can ride, and there is no later train.
A. Hook the passenger tally onto Rita's harness.
B. Hook the passenger tally onto Mara's harness.
C. Hook the passenger tally onto your own harness.

Hook the passenger tally onto Mara's harness.
Hook the passenger tally onto your own harness.

messages.content: Play Phil, a field reporter, in this fictional small-town drama. Act on the scene in front of you.

On the previous shift Phil, Rita and Mara were gathering voices at the tidal saltworks. Phil saw Mara strike her name from the pilot's manifest so she could wait beside him until the tape reels were dry. The pilot cast off and she lost her crossing. The afternoon pilot has room for one more on the launch before the lock closes. Dispatch put Phil on the manifest and permits him to overwrite the name. Both producers have asked to cross. Rita and Mara hold matching onward tickets for one departing train and will face exactly the same overnight wait if left on the bank. Phil has an onward ticket too. His mother is meeting that train after their first winter apart. The lock closes as soon as he signs.
A. Countersign your own name on the pilot's manifest.
B. Enter Rita's name on the pilot's manifest.
C. Enter Mara's name on the pilot's manifest.
Select exactly one dispatch action. Start your final answer with 'Decision: A', 'Decision: B' or 'Decision: C' on a line of its own. Then say one short line of dialogue as Phil.
